actual_findings.description: The function opens the connection with conn.open() but now returns retry(query) without closing it. Restore the try/finally structure so conn.close() is always called, for example: `try:
    return retry(query)
finally:
    conn.close()`.

actual_findings.description: The change converts a propagated ValueError into a None return value. Previously the exception was explicitly re-raised, indicating that callers were expected to observe the failure. After this change, any caller that relies on emit() raising to detect an invalid event or callback result will instead continue execution with a None result, which can lead to unchecked None dereferences, incorrect state updates, or silently dropped events. The failure is also indistinguishable from a callback that legitimately returns None.
actual_findings.suggested_remediation: Restore `except ValueError: raise` to preserve the original error-propagation contract, or, if None is intentionally a sentinel for failure, update every caller to check for it explicitly and ensure the callback's normal return type cannot legitimately be None.
actual_findings.title: ValueError is silently swallowed and replaced with None

actual_findings.description: Changing the loop condition to `start <= len(items)` allows the loop to execute when `start` equals the number of items. actual_findings.suggested_remediation: Restore the condition to `while start < len(items):`, or explicitly avoid invoking the callback when the remaining slice is empty.

Because `worker` appends to this list in place, repeated calls such as `worker(barrier=barrier)` accumulate multiple `'ready'` entries and return the shared list, causing callers to observe stale state from previous invocations.
candidate_findings.suggested_remediation: Use `pending=None` and initialize a fresh list inside the function: `pending = [] if pending is None else pending`.
candidate_findings.title: Mutable default list causes state to persist across worker calls

actual_findings.description: The implementation was changed from delegating to BasePolicy.authorize(user) to unconditionally returning True. As a result, InternalPolicy bypasses the inherited authorization checks and permits every user, including users that the base policy would reject.
actual_findings.suggested_remediation: Restore the base-policy delegation (`return super().authorize(user)`) or explicitly validate that the user is an authorized internal user before returning True.
actual_findings.title: InternalPolicy now authorizes every user

actual_findings.description: The callback registered with the bus is self.callback, which was assigned to self.on_event in __init__. close() instead passes a newly created lambda to bus.off(). Since this lambda is a different object from the registered callback, the original listener is not removed. The controller remains subscribed after close, continues processing events, and may be retained by the bus.
actual_findings.suggested_remediation: Remove the exact callback that was registered: `self.bus.off(self.callback)`.
actual_findings.title: close() does not remove the registered event callback

actual_findings.description: The previous try/finally guaranteed that `source.close()` ran when the generator completed, raised, or was closed. After this change, `chunks` only reads from the source and never releases it. Unless every caller independently closes the source, file handles, connections, or other resources can remain open, and an exception from `source.read()` also bypasses cleanup.
actual_findings.title: Generator no longer closes the source resource
